identity.title: AutoGFM: Automated Graph Foundation Model with Adaptive Architecture Customization

problem.claim: The paper addresses how to customize graph foundation model architectures across diverse graph domains and tasks.

gap.claim: Existing graph foundation models use hand-designed, fixed GNN architectures and therefore do not adapt architecture choice to specific domains and tasks.

contributions.claim: AutoGFM discovers an invariant graph–architecture relationship and combines disentangled contrastive encoding, invariant-guided customization, and curriculum architecture customization.
The paper provides a theoretical analysis of limitations in existing graph neural architecture search.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that they explore graph neural architecture search for graph foundation models for the first time.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show AutoGFM outperforms baselines and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph foundation models seek to transfer graph knowledge across domains and tasks, but existing models rely on fixed, hand-designed architectures.
The paper frames graph neural architecture search for foundation models as challenged by architecture inconsistency: optimal architectures vary across domains and tasks.
AutoGFM targets an invariant graph–architecture relationship through pattern disentanglement, adaptive customization, and curriculum-based search control.
The authors report superior performance to baselines in extensive experiments.

source_observation.claim: The abstract maps three explicitly named search challenges to three corresponding mechanisms: disentangled encoding, invariant-guided customization, and curriculum customization.

lessons.interpretation: A contribution can be easier to assess when each stated obstacle has a visibly paired design response.
lessons.application: For a multi-factor method, enumerate the central challenges and state one mechanism or analysis component addressing each.
lessons.exception: This mapping may be unsuitable when the proposed components are tightly coupled or when the work has only one dominant challenge.

unknowns: The abstract does not report datasets, task counts, numerical gains, baseline identities, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not provide details of the theoretical analysis or establish the claimed firstness independently.
